In order to evaluate the BER under its mission scenarios in an efficient way, the paper analyzes the BER model for wireless networks, derives the BER similar criteria based on similarity theory and establishes the accelerated models. This accelerated model is verified on a wireless network based on simulation platform. The results show that the BER in normal original network and the similar network are almost the same.

articleTitle: 2D ISAR imaging scheme in complex baseband echo domain based on compressive sensing
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) theory asserts that one can recover original signals from far fewer random samples under the condition of sparse signals. In this paper, CS technique is applied to ISAR imaging. An imaging scheme based on far fewer random samples in ISAR complex baseband echo domain is proposed. Joint 2D imaging processing without translational motion compensation can be achieved. The data rate and complexity of radar imaging system can be effectively reduced. The effectiveness of the imaging scheme is tested through processing simulated data.

articleTitle: A new pattern of MIMO radar GMTI
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: Utilizing digital beam forming (DBF) on transmit and receive, the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar can be applied to ground moving target indication (GMTI) and can provide an efficient way to improve the GMTI performance. The operating pattern is very significant for the MIMO radar GMTI. For the traditional GMTI pattern, there is a conflict of the wider swath and narrower clutter bandwidth. The observation area can be broadened with MIMO techniques by scanning. This paper designs an effective pattern with the simultaneous transmission of multi-phase-centre multi-sub-band signals as well as beam scanning in each pulse, which provide an efficient way to settle the conflict. By beam scanning in pulse, the new pattern has wider azimuth swath, shorter revisiting period, larger coherent processing interval (CPI) number and higher SCNR. By MIMO technology, more equivalent phase centres and longer efficient baselines can be formed, so the performance of GMTI can be improved. The principle of space-time-frequency adaptive processing (STFAP) is analysed, simulation results are presented to prove the superiority of MIMO radar in clutter suppression and GMTI. Analysis of the results indicates improved detection performance with the new pattern compared to the conventional approach.

articleTitle: An abnormal file access behavior detection approach based on file path diversity
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: Information security is a great challenge for organizations in our modern information world. Existing security facilities like Firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems and Antivirus are not enough to guarantee the security of information. File is an important carrier of information, which is the intent of quite a number of attackers, in this paper, we propose an FPD-based approach for detecting abnormal file access behaviours. FPD (File Path Diversity) is a quantized value which measures how far a set of file paths is spread out, and in which abnormal file access behaviours and normal ones show significant differences, making it an effective indicator for detecting malicious processes that controlled by attackers to search and steal valuable files. An algorithm of calculating FPD values is presented, as well as a prototype system based on FPD for detecting malicious processes. Experiments demonstrate that FPD is very effective in detecting malicious processes with abnormal file access behaviours, we get a best result of a100% Detection Rate and a 3.85% False Positive Rate.

articleTitle: Multi-sensor fusion recognition method based on improved D-S evidence theory
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: A multi-sensor fusion recognition method based on improved D-S evidence theory is presented in this paper to solve the problem of highly conflictive multi-sensor fusion recognition in the decision fusion of target comprehensive recognition system which D-S evidence theory can't solve. The method modifies evidence sources by calculating the weights using the resemblance degree of single characteristic recognition results, then handle the fusion processing of the modified evidence sources to get comprehensive recognition results. The numerical example analyses demonstrate the superiority of the method proposed in this paper that it can effectively improve the accuracy and reliability of the combination. And the last simulation results of the missile target integrated recognition indicate that this method can effectively solve the problem of high conflictive data fusion error existing in the decision fusion process and improve the recognition performance of the recognition system perfectly.

articleTitle: A low complexity PTS algorithm for controlling PAPR of OFDM signals
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: This paper presents an improved suboptimum PTS algorithm controlling the Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) of the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals. The phase factors are divided into several parts. Under other parts unchanged the optimal combination is found in one part, and repeated in others. The final combination of phase factors consists of the optimal combinations of each part. The PAPR performance of this method is close to the optimal PTS, but the amount of calculation is much smaller. This algorithm reduces PAPR by finding the optimal combinations of phase factors in each part. The method of dividing the phase factors is very flexible. The emulations show that this algorithm can reduce the PAPR of the OFDM system more effectively at the same amount of calculation.

articleTitle: A CPK-based privacy enhanced key exchange scheme for vehicular mesh network
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: Most of the existing vehicle networks use PKI technology to issue the certificate and key for the user, but with a sharp increasing, there will be higher computational overhead and transmission overhead in the communication by using PKI. It would seriously hamper the development of vehicle networks. Therefore, this paper proposes a combined public key(CPK)-based privacy enhanced key exchange scheme through which public key is closely bound to the identity of the vehicle in vehicular mesh network. When the nodes belong to different clusters, the scheme provides the mutual authentication between mesh client and mesh router to make network securer. Compared to the existing scheme, the scheme could withstand the modification attack and the man in-the-middle attack.

articleTitle: A cross-layer adaptive incremental cooperative relaying scheme for wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: In wireless sensor networks, the traditional incremental cooperative relaying scheme (IR) could improve the system throughput enormously over fading channels by exploiting relay nodes to retransmit the source data packet to the destination. In order to enhance the system throughput over time-varying fading channels, this paper proposes an adaptive incremental cooperative relaying scheme (AIR) based on adaptive modulation and coding, which implements adaptive rate transmission for the source and relay nodes according to channel state information. We derive expressions for the AIR system throughput, and then give a gradient-based search algorithm to find the optimized adaptive solution for the AIR system by maximizing throughput subject to the constraint of packet error rate at the data link layer. The results indicate that throughput of AIR system outperforms that of traditional IR system greatly for any SNR value.

articleTitle: Joint cell association, component carrier selection and beamforming on carrier aggregated channels in heterogeneous networks
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: This paper considers the joint cell association, component carrier selection and beamforming on carrier aggregated channels in Heterogeneous Networks. The problem is modelled as a sum rate maximization problem with constraints and is solved by a successive allocation update algorithm. The proposed algorithm starts with a cell association stage in which the serving cell will be decided with an objective of maximizing the network sum rate while simultaneously minimizing the sum of interference power towards the other cells, then in the next stage, the beamforming and carrier selection will be iteratively carried out. The beamforming is achieved by a signal-to-weighted-leakage plus-noise ratio, afterwards, carrier selection is used to shut down a subset of the component carrier in order to allow for a perfect interference removal at the receive side in the large dense low power node deployment scenario. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm not only exploits additional degrees of freedom provided by multiple antennas and component carriers, but also ensures that the inter- and intra-cell interference will not overwhelm the cell-splitting gains.

articleTitle: Integrated band voltage controlled oscillator and mixer with LNA for wireless communications
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: A simple low phase noise and wide tuning range voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) and mixer with charge injection designed for 10 GHz band application. The proposed oscillator adopts a complementary cross-coupled pair LC-VCO circuit with only one symmetrical inductor and implemented in TSMC 0.18-um CMOS process. At the supply voltage of 1.8 V, measured results achieve a tuning range of 9.6 to 11.08 GHz, corresponding to 13.9 %, a phase noise under −115.1 dBc/Hz at a 1 MHz offset frequency from 10.02 GHz with a tuned control voltage from 0 to 1.7 V and an output power of −2.231 dBm at 50-Ω termination and at 10.02 GHz. The proposed broadband CMOS double-balance mixer for wireless receiver is presented. Measurement of the CMOS mixer is performed using an integrated fixture. In the communicated low-band, input return loss is higher than 8.5 dB. The proposed VCO, without the need of any off-chip device, is well suitable for the networking integration of wireless systems.

articleTitle: Minimal sampling for direction of arrival estimation using finite rate of innovation principle
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: Many high resolution DOA estimation techniques have been achieved for decades, most of which depend on a large sampling. However, restricted by the sampling time or the sensor elements, the samples are usually not enough in many applications. This leads us to consider the minimal sampling for the DOA estimation, under which the DOA can not be estimated correctly. Our goal is to determine the sampling bound and to develop the corresponding estimation method. When the noise is small, we also consider the sufficient condition for the DOA estimation with different structures of the signal sources.

articleTitle: BER performance analysis of distributed antenna systems over composite channels
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: In this paper, the downlink bit error rate (BER) performance of distributed antenna systems (DAS) with antenna selection over a composite fading channel is presented, where path loss, Rayleigh fading and lognormal shadowing are all considered for practicability. According to the performance analysis, and using the gamma distribution to approach log-normal distribution, an approximate closed-form expression of average BER is derived. This expression has a simple form and the value close to the actual simulation. To improve the accuracy of the BER further, we also derive a tightly approximate expression of cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the effective signal to noise ratio (SNR) by employing the numerical integrals. Based on this CDF, a tightly-approximate BER expression is achieved. All these theoretical expressions will provide good performance evaluation for DAS downlink. Simulation results show that the derived BER expressions are effective, and can match the corresponding simulations well, especially the second BER expression.

articleTitle: Modeling message dissemination in Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANET), a sub-section of Ad Hoc Networks, are composed by vehicles with wireless devices which can communicate to other vehicles and roadside infrastructure. One of important application is to improve traffic congestion by disseminate accident message as soon as possible. Therefore, the diffusion of an accident alert, is critical. Predicting traffic message diffusion opens an opportunity to adopt appropriate strategies to manage traffic, vacuum vehicles from disasters, or recovery from accidents. But Modeling data dissemination is challenging due to vehicles' high mobility, which results rapidly changing network topologies. This paper addresses information diffusion models in vehicular networks. We analytically investigate time-critical information diffusion

articleTitle: Ripley's K based analysis of base station distribution
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: In recent years, as the fast growth of the mobile users, network coverage area becomes larger, then so does the number of base stations (BSs). Therefore, how to predict network coverage scientifically and effectively, how to project base station construction and how to make the best effect of the base station network coverage are to be solved urgently. However, the selection of the base station location has a great impact on the performance and maintenance of the network. Hence, the correct siting of the base stations is the key to the wireless network planning. Based on the real data of the city and suburb, the characteristic of heterogeneous network base stations is analyzed in this paper. The more rational and accurate completion of the base station location is determined by the distributed model of the base station.

articleTitle: A new dynamic updating key strategy based on EMSA in wireless mesh networks
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: In the security protocols of Efficient Mesh Security Association(EMSA), the key updating strategy is an effective method to ensure the security of communication. For the existing strategy of periodic automatic key updating, the PTK(Pairwise Transit Key) is updated through the complex 4-way handshake to produce each time. Once the update frequency of the PTK is faster, it will have a greater impact on throughput and delay of the network. On this basis, we propose a new strategy of dynamic key updating to ensure the safety and performance of wireless mesh networks. In the new strategy, mesh point(MP) and mesh authenticator(MA) negotiate a random function at the initial certification, and use the PTK which is generated by the 4-way handshake as the initial seed. When the PTK updating cycle comes, both sides generate the new keys using the random function, which do not have to generate a new PTK by complex 4-way handshake. The analysis of performance compared with existing strategies showed that the dynamic key updating strategy proposed in this paper have a larger increase in delay and throughput of the network.

articleTitle: A note on weight distributions of irreducible cyclic codes
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: Usually, it is difficult to determine the weight distribution of an irreducible cyclic code. In this paper, we discuss the case that an irreducible cyclic code has the maximal number of distinct nonzero weights and give a necessary and sufficient condition. In this case, we also obtain a divisible property for the weight of a codeword. Further, we present a necessary and sufficient condition for an irreducible cyclic code with only one nonzero weight. Finally, we determine the weight distribution of an irreducible cyclic code for some cases.

articleTitle: Asymptotic performance analysis of multiuser MIMO system in Rayleigh fading channels
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: In this paper, the bit error rate (BER) performance of multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems over Rayleigh fading channels is studied, and corresponding asymptotic performance is analyzed. Based on the asymptotic analysis at high signal to noise ratio (SNR), using the probability density functions (PDF) of the instantaneous channel power gain, the diversity gain and coding gain of the system with transmit antenna selection (TAS) scheme and space-time block coding (STBC) scheme are derived, respectively. As a result, the same full diversity gain is achieved for two transmission schemes, but their coding gains are different. With the obtained diversity gain and coding gain, the asymptotic BER expressions for two transmission schemes are respectively derived, which are in good agreement with the corresponding simulation results. The results show that the multiuser MIMO system with TAS scheme has better BER performance than that with STBC scheme due to higher coding gain.

articleTitle: Vertex-cut based topology repair in wireless sensor and actuator networks
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: In Wireless Sensor and Actuator Networks (WSANs), the good connectivity is one of the most important prerequisites to ensure them working properly. Especially for the inter-actuator networks in WSANs, the connectivity is crucial for actuators to cooperate with each other to execute tasks correctly and efficiently. The paper proposes a Vertex-cut based Topology Repair algorithm (CVTR) which can maintain the connectivity of inter-actuator networks through relocating one-hop neighbors of failure nodes. The simulation experiment results show that CVTR can more effectively repair the connectivity of inter-actuator networks with much lower coverage loss and less number of nodes moved, comparing with the important and typical algorithm RIM.

articleTitle: A low-time-delay scheduling algorithm for Video on Demand service over P2P networks
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Information and Communications Technologies (ICT 2014)
abstract: We are interested in providing Video-on-Demand (VoD) streaming service to a large population of clients using peer-to-peer (P2P) approach. One of the drawbacks of the current P2P architectures is that which have long start-up delays. In this paper, a novel scheme is envisioned to effectively provide a Video-on-Demand (VoD) over P2P networks. The scheme covers three main methods, namely first copying, grouping based on parts and priority scheduling. In fact, all above phases work synchronously to achieve a good performance. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that this new scheduling algorithm not only achieves low start-up time and high streaming continuity but also keeps a good network throughput even in hard network conditions.
